walkthroughs.body_html:
Henry VIII & His Ministers 1509-40 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Henry VIII & His Ministers 1509-40 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Henry VIII & His Ministers 1509-40.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who led the Pilgrimage of Grace in 1536?
options: Robert Aske
Thomas More
Reginald Pole
Thomas Wyatt

mcqs.q: When was the Act of Supremacy passed?
Why did Henry VIII break with Rome?
options: William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Because he wanted England to become Protestant.
Primarily for an annulment from Catherine of Aragon, but also to seize Church wealth and assert royal supremacy — not for Protestant theological reasons.

mcqs.q: Why did Henry II clash with Thomas Becket?
options: They quarrelled because Becket wanted to be Pope.
Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Becket resisted Henry's attempt to bring 'criminous clerks' under royal courts via the Constitutions of Clarendon, defending Church independence from royal jurisdiction.
Henry II ordered Becket's assassination personally.

mcqs.q: Why did William of Normandy claim the English throne in 1066?
options: William invaded because he was the strongest king in Europe and wanted more land.
They quarrelled because Becket wanted to be Pope.
William was Edward the Confessor's eldest son.
He claimed Edward the Confessor had promised him the throne in 1051 and that Harold Godwinson had sworn an oath to support that claim in 1064.
